learning_objective: 🎯 Unravel the mysteries of invisible electricity, learn how it flows through circuits, and explore how it creates heat and magnetism!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Electricity is like a flow of invisible energy. For it to power our TVs or bulbs, it needs an unbroken path to travel on. This closed, circular pathway made of wires, batteries, and a switch is called an electric circuit.

When electrical energy struggles to squeeze through certain thin wires, the wire gets really hot and starts glowing! This is how electric room heaters, toasters, and the filament inside traditional light bulbs work.

Electricity has a secret superpower: it can act like a magnet! When electricity flows through a wire coiled around an iron nail, the nail temporarily turns into an electromagnet, attracting other metal objects.

fun_activity.title: 🔦 Be a Circuit Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Safely examine a simple battery-operated toy flashlight at home with an adult. Try to identify the battery (power source), the tiny bulb, and how the on/off switch opens and closes the circuit to let the electricity flow!

quick_recap: ⭐ An electric circuit must be closed and unbroken for current to flow.
⭐ Electricity passing through a high-resistance wire creates heat.
⭐ Flowing electricity can create powerful temporary magnets called electromagnets.
